title: चार कक्षामा अध्ययनरत विद्यार्थीहरूको सस्वरपठन क्षमताको अध्ययन{Study of Reading Ability of Students Studying in Class Four}
nepali: शोधशीर्षक ः चार कक्षामा अध्ययनरत विद्यार्थीहरूको सस्वरपठन क्षमताको अध्ययनशोधार्थी ः हरी गिरीशोधनिर्देशक ः उप प्रा.श्री राजेन्द्रप्रसाद पौडेलविभाग÷क्याम्पस ः नेपाली भाषा शिक्षा विभाग, विश्वविद्यालय क्याम्पस, कीर्तिपुरशैक्षिक वष ः २०६०÷०६२; पृष्ठ ः ११६+१३ ः जम्मा अध्याय ः पाँच शोधप्रक्रियाप्रस्तुत शोधपत्र नेपाली शिक्षा एम. एड. दास्रो वष नेपा. शि. ५९८ पाठयांशका प्रयोजनका लागि तयार गरिएको हो ।कक्षा चारमा अध्ययनरत विद्यार्थीहरूको सस्वरपठन क्षमताको अध्ययन गर्ने, भाषाका विद्यार्थीहरूको सस्वरपठन क्षमता पहिल्याउने, विद्यार्थीहरूका सस्वरपठन सम्वन्धी समस्या र तिनको कारण पत्ता लगाउने, उपरोक्त समस्या समाधानका लागि आवश्यक सुझावहरू प्रस्तुतगर्ने उद्देश्यमा प्रस्तुत शोधकार्य केन्द्रित रहेको छ । यस शोधकार्यमा क्षेत्रीय सामग्री सङकलन विधिको अवलम्बन गरिएको छ । त्यसक्रममा पर्वत जिल्लाका बाँसखर्क, माझफाँट, लेकफाँट, धाइरिङ्ग, नाग्लिवाङ, पाङ, खुर्काेट रशिवालय गरी ८ गा. वि. स. लाई सामग्री सङकलनको स्रोत क्षेत्र बनाइएको छ । यसरीप्रश्नावली फाराममा विभिन्न उपशीर्षक राखी प्रश्नावलीका साथै मौखिक अन्तर्वाता,अनौपचारिक कुराकानी आदि प्रयोगात्मक पद्धतिद्वारा आवश्यक सामग्री सङकलन गरिएका देखिन्छ । यस पद्धतिमा सूचकहरू विद्यार्थीहरूलाई नै गराइएको छ । पहिलो अध्यायमा शोध परिचय, दोस्रोमा सस्वरपठनको सैद्धान्तिक अवधारण, तेस्रोमाव्याख्या तथा विल्लेषण, चौथोमा सस्वरपठनमा देखिएका समस्या र पाँचौमा निष्कर्ष र सुझाव गरी पाँच अध्यायमा यो शोधपत्र तयार भएको छ । शोध निष्कर्षयस शोधका मुख्य निष्कर्षहरूलाई निम्नानुसार प्रस्तुत गर्न सकिन्छ– १. ससस्वपठन भनेको लिपी चिन्हहरूलाई आवाजमा परिणत गर्नु हो ।२. यसलाई गतियति, पदयाग, पदवियोग, हाउभाउ, विधाको ख्याल, आरोहअवरोह, चिन्हका ख्याल, बोधगम्यता, उच्चारण, शब्द र वाक्यको पनरावृत्ति, थेगो र मातृभाषाका प्रभावआदि शीर्षकमा राखी अध्ययन गरिएको छ । ३. माथिका सबै शीर्षकहरूमा जातिगत रुपमा दमाई, कामी, गुरुङ, मगर आदि जातिहरू नराम्रो स्थितिमा देखिएका छन भने ब्राह्मण, क्षेत्री, राम्रो स्तरमा देखिएका छन । ४. अधिकांश विद्यालयका विद्यार्थीहरूले माथिका बुँदाहरू मध्ये चिन्हको ख्याल अरू बुँदाभन्दा राम्रो गरेको पाइया । अरू बुँदाहरू कमजोर स्तरमा छन।
american_english:
Research title: A Study of the Oral Reading Ability of Students in Class Four
Researcher: Hari Giri
Research adviser: Assistant Professor Rajendra Prasad Poudel
Department/campus: Department of Nepali Language Education, University Campus, Kirtipur
Academic year: 2060/62 BS; pages: 116+13; total chapters: five
Research procedure
This research paper was prepared to meet the requirement of the second-year M.Ed. course Nepa. Shi. 598 in Nepali Education.
The study is focused on examining the oral reading ability of students in class four, determining the oral reading ability of language students, identifying the problems students have with oral reading and their causes, and presenting the suggestions needed to resolve those problems.
This study adopted a field-based method of collecting materials.
In doing so, eight VDCs of Parbat district — Banshkhark, Majhphant, Lekhphant, Dhairing, Naglibang, Pang, Khurkot and Shivalaya — were used as the source area for data collection.
Materials were collected through a questionnaire form with various subheadings, along with oral interviews, informal conversations and other practical methods.
In this approach the indicators were administered directly to the students.
The paper is organized into five chapters: research introduction in the first, the theoretical concept of oral reading in the second, explanation and analysis in the third, the problems seen in oral reading in the fourth, and conclusions and suggestions in the fifth.
Research findings
The main findings of this study can be presented as follows:
1. Oral reading means converting written symbols into sound.
2. It was studied under the headings of speed, word separation, word combination, gestures, attention to style, rising and falling intonation, attention to punctuation, comprehension, pronunciation, repetition of words and sentences, refrain, and mother-tongue influence.
3. Under all these headings, caste groups such as Damai, Kami, Gurung and Magar were found in a poor position, while Brahmin and Kshetri were found at a good level.
4. Most students in the schools were found to pay better attention to punctuation than to the other points; the remaining points are at a weak level.
british_english:
Research title: A Study of the Oral Reading Competence of Pupils Studying in Class Four
Researcher: Hari Giri
Research supervisor: Assistant Professor Rajendra Prasad Poudel
Department/campus: Department of Nepali Language Education, University Campus, Kirtipur
Academic year: 2060/62 BS; pages: 116+13; total chapters: five
Research procedure
The present dissertation was prepared in fulfilment of the second-year M.Ed. course Nepa. Shi. 598 in Nepali Education.
This research work is centred on studying the oral reading competence of pupils in class four, ascertaining the oral reading competence of language pupils, identifying the difficulties pupils encounter with oral reading and their causes, and putting forward the suggestions required to address the above difficulties.
A field-based method of material collection has been adopted in this research work.
In that connection, eight village development committees of Parbat district — Banshkhark, Majhphant, Lekhphant, Dhairing, Naglibang, Pang, Khurkot and Shivalaya — were made the source area for material collection.
It is apparent that the necessary material was gathered by means of a questionnaire containing various sub-headings, together with oral interviews, informal conversations and other empirical methods.
In this method, the indicators were administered to the pupils themselves.
This dissertation has been prepared in five chapters: research introduction in the first, the theoretical concept of oral reading in the second, explanation and analysis in the third, the problems observed in oral reading in the fourth, and conclusions and suggestions in the fifth.
Research conclusions
The principal conclusions of this research may be presented as follows:
1. Oral reading is the conversion of script symbols into sound.
2. It has been studied under the headings of pace, word separation, word conjunction, gesture, regard for style, intonation, regard for punctuation, comprehensibility, pronunciation, repetition of words and sentences, refrain and the influence of the mother tongue.
3. Across all the above headings, castes such as Damai, Kami, Gurung and Magar were seen to be in an unfavourable position, whereas Brahmin and Kshetri were seen to be at a favourable level.
4. Pupils in most schools were found to show better regard for punctuation than for the other points; the other points remain at a weak level.

informal_english:
Research title: How Well Do Class-Four Kids Read Out Loud?
Researcher: Hari Giri
Adviser: Assistant Prof. Rajendra Prasad Poudel
Department/campus: Nepali Language Education, University Campus, Kirtipur
Academic year 2060/62 BS; 116+13 pages; five chapters
How the research was done
This paper was written for the second-year M.Ed. Nepali Education course, Nepa. Shi. 598.
The whole point was to look at how well class-four kids read out loud, figure out where language students stand with reading aloud, find out what problems they run into and why, and suggest what to do about those problems.
For this study I went out and collected material in the field.
What that looked like: eight VDCs in Parbat district — Banshkhark, Majhphant, Lekhphant, Dhairing, Naglibang, Pang, Khurkot and Shivalaya — were the source area.
I used a questionnaire with different subheadings, plus oral interviews, casual chats and other hands-on methods to get what I needed.
The indicators were given straight to the students themselves.
The paper runs five chapters: introduction to the research first, the theory behind oral reading second, explanation and analysis third, the problems that showed up in oral reading fourth, and conclusions and suggestions fifth.
What the research found
The main findings are:
1. Reading out loud just means turning written symbols into sound.
2. The study looked at speed, separating words, joining words, gestures, paying attention to style, intonation, watching punctuation, comprehension, pronunciation, repeating words and sentences, refrains and mother-tongue influence.
3. On every one of those headings, Dalit and Janajati groups like Damai, Kami, Gurung and Magar came out worse, while Brahmin and Kshetri came out better.
4. Most students did a better job with punctuation than with the other points, and the other points are still weak.
